feedback: If a child recites 3s with no sense of grouping, lay out the arrays or counters so each jump matches a visible group of three.
Praise linking the jump count to the number of groups (e.g. 'five jumps, five threes, fifteen').
activities.intendedInsight: Each step of 3 is one more group of three; stepping in 3s is the foundation of the 3× table and connects to thirds.
learnerActions: Make equal jumps of 3 along a number line, saying the multiple you land on each time.
For each jump, add one more group of three — show it with an array or counters (three counters per group) alongside the jump.
Connect 'four jumps of 3' to 'four groups of three' (four threes make 12) and to building up the 3× table.
Briefly link three equal groups making a whole to the idea of 'a third'.
activities.title: Number-line 3-jumps and groups of three

feedback: If backward counting collapses or reverts to forward, slow to short runs with physical hops back along the line — treat it as a distinct skill.
If a child restarts at 3 to continue a mid-sequence, model 'the step is always +3, so add 3 to the last number you were given' and practise from several starting points; do not mark this wrong.

If each next multiple is reached by sub-counting ones under the breath (18… 19, 20, 21), do NOT drill for speed; make the step visible with number-line jumps of 3 and the diagonal pattern, and let fluency grow with exposure.
activities.intendedInsight: Backward counting and continuing from any point are separate skills: the step is always +3 (or −3), so you can add or subtract 3 from the last number rather than restarting.
learnerActions: Count backwards in 3s from a multiple: 30, 27, 24… down to 0, using physical or drawn hops back along a number line.
Practise short backward runs (e.g. 12 → 0) as their own skill, not expecting it to come free with forward counting.
Continue a sequence from the middle: given 12, 15, 18, say the next number (and keep going) without restarting from 3.
Say the number just before a given multiple (e.g. what comes before 12 in the 3s).
activities.title: Counting back and entering mid-sequence

feedback: Correct answers confirm the step; errors signal where to return to the hundred square or number line (e.g. decade crossings or backward runs).
Oral partner counting gives backward-count practice and fluency; pair it with the seen diagonal pattern on a hundred square so the visible pattern reinforces the underlying idea.
activities.intendedInsight: Fluency means stepping by three both ways and entering the sequence at any point, not only chanting up from 0.
learnerActions: Answer quick questions: 'What is the next number in 3s?', fill a missing multiple in a sequence, put multiples of 3 in order, and count back in 3s.
With a partner, count aloud in 3s forwards and backwards, taking turns to say the next number.
Answer 'What's 3 more than 18?' (21) and 'What comes just before 12 in the 3s?' (9).
activities.title: Retrieval and oral fluency
